arxiv-2107-08991.title: A Tree Search Approach for Maximum-Likelihood Decoding of Reed-Muller Codes
arxiv-2107-08991.creator: Seyyed Ali Hashemi 1 , Nghia Doan 2 , Warren J. Gross 2 , John Cioffi 1 , Andrea Goldsmith 3
arxiv-2107-08991.description: Abstract A low-complexity tree search approach is presented that achieves the maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding performance of Reed-Muller (RM) codes. The proposed approach generates a bit-flipping tree that is traversed to find the ML decoding result by performing successive-cancellation decoding after each node visit.

arxiv-2203-11842.description: Abstract Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) is a powerful way of learning from demonstrations. In this paper, we address IRL problems with the availability of prior knowledge that optimal policies will never violate certain constraints. Conventional approaches ignoring these constraints need many demonstrations to converge.

arxiv-2302-11402.title: Cooperative melting in double-stranded peptide chains through local mechanical interactions
arxiv-2302-11402.creator: Luca Bellino, Giuseppe Florio, Alain Goriely, Giuseppe Puglisi
arxiv-2302-11402.description: Abstract Depending on the external field, double-stranded peptide chains can separate following a cooperative or non-cooperative transition strategy. arxiv-2303-05976.title: On the coherence of one-relator groups and their group algebras
arxiv-2303-05976.creator: Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Marco Linton
arxiv-2303-05976.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Marco Linton. We prove that one-relator groups are coherent, solving a well-known problem of Gilbert Baumslag. Our proof strategy is readily applicable to many classes of groups of cohomological dimension two. We show that fundamental groups of two complexes with non-positive immersions are homologically coherent, we show that groups with staggered presentations and many Coxeter groups are coherent and we show that group algebras over fields of characteristic zero of groups with reducible presentations without proper powers are coherent.

arxiv-2305-03301.description: Abstract In this work, we apply the concept about operator connection to consider bivariate random tensor means. pmc-11428019.title: Mortality in hospitalized SARS-CoV-2 patients with contemporaneous bacterial and fungal infections
pmc-11428019.creator: John J. Hanna, Zachary M. Most, Lauren N. Cooper, Abdi D. Wakene, Alexander P. Radunsky, Christoph U. Lehmann, Trish M. Perl, Richard J. Medford
pmc-11428019.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:The interplay between SARS-CoV-2 and contemporaneous bacterial or fungal culture growth may have crucial implications for clinical outcomes of hospitalized patients. This study aimed to quantify the effect of microbiological culture positivity on mortality among hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2.Methods:In this retrospective cohort study, we included adult hospitalized patients from OPTUM COVID-19 specific data set, who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 within 14 days of hospitalization between 01/20/2020 and 01/20/2022.

pmc-12935765.creator: Ebrahim Alijani, Mahboobeh Sabeti Akbar-Abad, Hossein Shahriari, Fatemeh Keykha, Mahdi Majidpour, Michael Faqih, Mohsen Taheri, Mahdi Atabaki
pmc-12935765.description: BackgroundPulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remains a significant global health challenge, necessitating a deeper understanding of genetic factors influencing susceptibility. pmc-13466910.title: Association of Glycemic Status with Disability, Relapse Activity, Inflammatory Markers, and Metabolic Profile in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis
pmc-13466910.creator: Soner Yeşilyurt, Furkan Talha Tokdemir, Mehmet Tayfur, Burcu Altunrende, Hafize Uzun
pmc-13466910.description: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysregulation has emerged as a potential modifier of disease activity and disability in multiple sclerosis (MS). However, the relationship between glycemic status and clinical outcomes in patients with MS remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of glycemic regulation with disease severity, relapse activity, inflammatory markers, and metabolic characteristics in patients with MS.

pmc-13720001.title: Whole-genome sequencing of 197 cases with Parkinson’s disease reveals novel pathogenic variants in the Indian population
pmc-13720001.creator: Hiba Ali, Banashree Mondal, Andie Pinto, Camellia Sarkar, Bikram Kumar Panda, Khader Valli Rupanagudi, Vikram V. Holla, Tarunya Nagaraj, Shubha GS Bhat, Shweta Prasad, Mahima Bhardwaj, Pooja Mailankody, Rohan R. Mahale, Nitish Kamble, Ravi Yadav, Pramod Kumar Pal, Albert Stezin, Latha Diwakar, Shwet
pmc-13720001.description: Most insights into the genetics of Parkinson’s disease (PD) arise from European cohorts, leaving the genomic diversity of India underexplored. To address this gap, we performed whole-genome sequencing of 197 Indian PD cases (106 with early-onset PD (EOPD) and 91 with late-onset PD (LOPD)), capturing SNVs, indels, splice, and structural variants.
